rationale: This is a tiny (9-line, 14-function) TSVC benchmark whose code is dominated by a 39.7KB init routine full of loop-heavy array code plus one hot search loop (s332), so size headroom and loop runtime are the binding constraints. SUB and SPLIT get high permissiveness weights (RuntimeCost/SizeCost/Risk 0.70-0.85) because they add strong static-analysis friction with near-zero cost and are safe on hot loops; IGV is moderately favored since the program's large global arrays make global indirection effective, and its per-access overhead is acceptable. FLA keeps the highest SecurityGain (0.75) as the strongest single deterrent, but its RuntimeCost weight is capped at 0.30 so the dispatcher-overhead dimension suppresses it on the hot search loop rather than on cold setup code; BCF is similarly security-valuable (0.70) but its SizeCost weight is held low (0.20) because bogus-control-flow cloning would balloon the already-dominant init body past an acceptable size budget. IBR is allowed only moderately (RuntimeCost 0.30) to spare the tight search loop from indirect-branch misprediction, and ICALL is kept near-disabled (all weights <=0.60, SecurityGain 0.40) because a program this small offers almost no call-graph surface to hide, so its indirection cost buys little. CorrectnessRisk weights are set high only for the provably semantics-preserving cheap passes, keeping the riskier control-flow transforms (FLA, IBR, BCF) selective rather than blanket-applied.
